hypothesis: c024 (score +0.715) validated criticality-weighted contrastive loss + criticality-aware area repair; c034's x2 penalty fine-tune (0.05→0.10) regressed slightly. Reverting the criticality shrink factor from 3.0 back toward a modest x0.5 value (3.0→1.5) keeps the proven mechanism but reduces the risk that shrinking critical macros' effective area over-tightens the balance repair (the failure mode seen in c026/c034), improving robustness across circuits.
expected_effect: WNS and TNS improve slightly or hold on all three cases (recovering c024-level ~+0.21 robust); overflow unchanged (~120–140); runtime unchanged.
analysis: The hypothesis held: reverting the criticality shrink factor to 1.5 preserved the proven contrastive-loss/area-repair mechanism while avoiding the over-tightening seen in c026/c034. All three cases improved (total +0.587, robust +0.146, min +0.135), with bp-ng45 gaining most (dTNS +37.7%, dWNS +7.3%) and bp_fe-ng45 the least (dWNS +18.0%, dTNS +10.0%). Overflow stayed moderate (~122–152), suggesting balance repair is no longer over-constrained. Next step: sweep shrink factor 1.0–2.0 across more circuits to confirm the robustness sweet spot before locking it in.
